definitions.gloss: following a precedent; carrying on unchanged
definitions.explanation: Continuing or adopting a policy, method, or practice that was established by a predecessor, without significant changes. Often used in political and organizational contexts.

examples.japanese: {前任者|ぜんにんしゃ}の{方針|ほうしん}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}する。
examples.english: To follow the policy of one's predecessor.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{社長|しゃちょう}は{前|まえ}の{経営|けいえい}{方針|ほうしん}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}すると{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The new president announced that he would carry on the previous management policy.

examples.japanese: {伝統|でんとう}をただ{踏襲|とうしゅう}するだけでなく、{時代|じだい}に{合|あ}わせて{変|か}えていくことも{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important not just to follow tradition but also to adapt to the times.

notes:
Compound of {踏|とう} (to tread upon) + {襲|しゅう} (to succeed to, to inherit). Literally "to walk in the same footsteps." Formal in tone, frequently used in news, politics, and business.

Can carry a neutral or slightly negative nuance depending on context — sometimes implying a lack of originality or unwillingness to reform.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {方針|ほうしん}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}する (follow a policy)
- {路線|ろせん}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}する (continue a course/direction)
- {伝統|でんとう}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}する (follow tradition)
- {前例|ぜんれい}を{踏襲|とうしゅう}する (follow precedent)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {継承|けいしょう}: inheriting and carrying on (more positive, emphasizes succession)
- {受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ: to inherit, to succeed to (broader, everyday usage)
